sentences.text: Misc .
Criminal Case No. 37678 of 2024

Rakesh Parmar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Mr. Tarun Kushwah - Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. Viraj Godha - P.L for the respondent/State.
 Order

This is first bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (now section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) for grant of bail to the applicant, relating to FIR/Crime No.287/2024 dated - (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Station Road, District - Ratlam (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420,406, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of the IPC.

2. Prosecution story in brief is that present applicant and co-accused persons committed cheating and criminal conspiracy with the complainant Devendra Singh and they have also committed forgery.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants/ accused persons submits that, the applicants have not committed the offence and have falsely been implicated in the case only on the basis of memorandum statement of co-accused Deepak Soni.
It is submitted that co-accused Deepak Soni has been granted bail by co- ordinate bench of this Court vide order dated 14.06.2024 passed in MCRC No. 23943/2024 who is main accused of the incident.
It is also submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26684 2 MCRC-37678-2024 the applicant is in custody since 17.07.2024.
No further custodial interrogation is required.
The trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that present applicant/accused be released on bail.

sentences.text: On other hand, learned counsel for the State/non-applicant has opposed the prayer and submitted that applicant has three criminal antecedents punishable under section IPC, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
However, it is fairly submitted that case of present applicant is identical with co-accused Deepak Soni.

5. Having considered the rival contentions of the learned counsels for the parties, perused the case diary, also looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the role as attributed by the applicant, this court is of considered view that this is a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Hence, without expressing any opinion on merit of the case, this application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant - RAKESH PARMAR be released on bail upon her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with solvent surety in the likewise amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section Section 480(3) of The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
6. The petitioner will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, this bail application is allowed and stands disposed of.
A copy of this order be sent to the Court below for compliance.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
